gloss: to deal with; to take notice of; to engage with

definitions.gloss: to deal with; to take notice of; to engage with; to pay attention to
definitions.explanation: To engage with or respond to someone. Very commonly used in the negative to mean ignoring someone or not giving them attention.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}にしないほうがいい。
だれも{彼|かれ}を{相手|あいて}にしなかった。
examples.english: Nobody paid any attention to him.

examples.japanese: そんなくだらない{挑発|ちょうはつ}を{相手|あいて}にする{必要|ひつよう}はない。
examples.english: There's no need to engage with such petty provocation.

notes:
USAGE:
Most frequently used in the negative ({相手|あいて}にしない) to mean "to ignore" or "to not bother with." In the affirmative, it can mean to engage with, respond to, or deal with someone. Also used with を: ～を{相手|あいて}にする.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～を{相手|あいて}にする (to deal with ~)
- {相手|あいて}にしない (to ignore, to not engage)
- {相手|あいて}にされない (to be ignored)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無視|むし}する: to ignore — more direct and deliberate
- {取|と}り{合|あ}う: to deal with, to attend to — can also be used in negative for ignoring
